messages.subject: Maxquant output converter function

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Maxquant output converter function
parts:
Dear Brett,

Using LFQ as input to MSstats is inappropriate.

As far as I understand, LFQ is calculated by (1) calculating a ratio of peptide intensity for all pairs of samples and all peptides that are shared between the pairs, (2) for each pair of samples, calculating the median protein ratio over the peptides, (3) take the protein ratios above for all pairs of samples as input to a system of linear equations, and estimate the individual protein abundances in each sample using least squares, and (4) rescale the resulting values to preserve the total intensity of the protein over all the samples.

As you can see, the values of LFQ are obtain by a joint analysis of all the data that pertain to this protein in the experiment. Therefore, the assumptions of MSstats (at least, these of independence) are not appropriate. Since the values of LFQ are already 'consensus' estimates obtained by least squares, the MSstats workflow on these values will underestimate the actual variability in the data and will lead to overly optimistic results.

HTH
Olga
